problem:
Change the order of integration in the following integral, 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dy\,dx.
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ then $x.$

feedback.problem:
Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{tan}⁡y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ and then $z.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z),$ ${u}_{2}(x,z),$ ${v}_{1}(z),$ ${v}_{2}(z),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{tan}⁡y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{4},\,\,0\le z\le \frac{\pi }{4},\,\,0\le x\le \operatorname{tan}⁡y}
$$

Now, let's sketch the region. Since it is a type II region, we first sketch the projection onto the $yz$-plane, given by

$$
E={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{4},\,\,0\le z\le \frac{\pi }{4}}.
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14095567/assets/e32a019900b77c0bb84b4599b8899e3d0d32ae07d9674da126db34394b97ea24.png)

Then, the region $R$ is shown in the diagram below, where $0\le x\le \operatorname{tan}⁡y.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14095567/assets/af629672ff2fd31eeae585ad4941fb8682941444cd34383392fb0a6bec24396e.png)

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type II *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14095567/assets/04dc917237ab002263e35fb4a84c264fef240fefaa456c5249d6e24d0c8ebe28.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
x=\operatorname{tan}⁡y\,⟹\,y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x.
$$

- The right boundary of the region is

$$
y=\frac{\pi }{4}.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,\operatorname{arctan}⁡x\le y\le \frac{\pi }{4}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14095567/assets/b2a6fc02441bb6013b6f54d49ceefafc1468b291ae4149847290135bbf2d2e56.png)

We now consider the projection $D$ as a type II plane region in the $xz$-plane with the top curve given by 

$$
x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=1.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14095567/assets/b942dbfba8276421620df6258c9951c2b91a5d2dea18c84260c90b6cbe6f760b.png)

Hence, we have that

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le \frac{\pi }{4}}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ then $z,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{tan}⁡y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{arctan}⁡x}^{\pi /4}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$
